q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID,ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT J JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON E.EMPLOYEE_ID = J.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID,ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT J JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON E.EMPLOYEE_ID = J.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries compute the average experience years of employees per project by joining the PROJECT and EMPLOYEE tables on EMPLOYEE_ID and grouping by PROJECT_ID. The only differences are in the table aliases (A and B vs. J and E), which do not affect the result.
